question: What sum will earn a simple interest of ₹1,056 in 3 years at 16% per year rate of interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Rate of Interest** = 16% × 3 = 48%

Given, 48% of **Principal** = ₹1,056

**Principal** (100%) = (1056 ÷ 48) × 100 = 22 × 100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = ₹1,056

**Time** (T) = 3 years

**Rate** (R) = 16% per annum

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cc76775864b7c74816723027fef21834f1c42be8fe124bc7ca6212ea96f45db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1056 = (P × 16 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 1056 = (P × 48) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (1056 × 100) ÷ 48

⇒ P = 22 × 100

⇒ P = 2200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total **Amount** (A) at the end of the period is the sum of **Principal** and **Interest**: A = P + SI = P[1 + (RT/100)].

Rule of Simple Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant for every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Effective Rate Method

Effective Rate = R × T. This helps in directly calculating the **Interest** or **Principal** using percentage comparison.
